proved_components.Critical hexagon attainment: The normal and vertex parameters of enclosing hexagons with bounded area lie in a compact coordinate box. Nondegeneracy follows from closed incidence/strip constraints. A continuous determinant objective attains the hexagon-area infimum.

proved_components.Static critical-hexagon normalization: The attained hexagon has area and covolume 2*sqrt(3), and the explicit area-preserving map sends its six side midpoints to the sixth roots of unity. proved_components.Critical hexagon nondegeneracy: Every critical hexagon of the constructed minimizer has six genuine sides. proved_components.Critical midpoint contacts: An exact side-variation formula and convex separation prove that every side midpoint of every critical hexagon of the constructed minimizer lies on its boundary. No nondegeneracy or midpoint-membership assumptions remain in this theorem.
proved_components.Inscribed regular hexagon: The six regular roots of unity lie on the frontier of initiallyNormalizedMinimizer. Their convex hull is an inscribed regular hexagon. Full midpoint coverage and global order are proved separately in CriticalMidpointCoverage and CriticalMidpointOrder.
proved_components.Unique support at critical midpoints: The exact side variation fixing a midpoint has a strictly negative quadratic area change for a distinct supporting normal. Criticality therefore gives a unique normalized supporting form at every critical midpoint. Every nonzero supporting functional there is a positive scalar multiple of the side normal.
proved_components.Continuous normal on critical midpoint s: The critical midpoint set is the continuous image of the compact critical-hexagon parameter family. It includes all six midpoints of every critical hexagon and lies in the minimizer frontier. Uniqueness makes the normal coefficients constant on the fibers of the midpoint projection; compactness makes this projection a quotient map, proving continuity of the normalized support normal on this set. No full-boundary coverage or Lipschitz estimate follows from this theorem.
proved_components.Critical hexagon unique at a midpoint: The geometric critical hexagon is unique at a shared midpoint, irrespective of labels or orientation. After matching orientations, area fixes the transverse coordinate of the next midpoint. The two neighboring supporting-strip inequalities force its remaining displacement to vanish; uniqueness of support normals then identifies all three strips. This proves existence and uniqueness of a critical hexagon region on the critical midpoint set, without asserting full boundary coverage.
proved_components.Supporting faces meet critical contacts: Symmetric slab cuts with levels tending to one contain explicit homothetic inner approximations. Irreducibility gives smaller enclosing hexagons and excluded points. Compactness yields a limiting critical hexagon and a contact on the original supporting face. This proves contact at exposed points, without assuming boundary regularity.
proved_components.Contact locus determines the minimizing: Every nonzero linear functional attains its maximum over the constructed minimizer at a critical contact. Separation then proves that the closed convex hull of the critical contact set equals the minimizing body. Equality of this closed convex hull does not assert full boundary coverage by contacts.
proved_components.Critical midpoint in every supporting fa: A support form of a symmetric slab cut at a point strictly inside the slab supports the original convex body, by a short convex-segment argument. Minimum enclosing hexagons of cuts converge to a strict critical hexagon. Their side midpoints lie on the cut boundaries. If all limiting midpoints avoided the shaved faces, locality would force the smaller hexagons to enclose the original body. Thus every supporting face contains a critical midpoint.
proved_components.Full critical-edge coverage of the bound: A normalized support form for any boundary point also supports a critical midpoint in its face. Uniqueness at that midpoint identifies the form with the side normal of a critical hexagon. Thus every boundary point lies on an edge of a critical hexagon: criticalContactSet equals the entire frontier. This does not yet assert that every boundary point is a side midpoint.
proved_components.No corners on the minimizing body: Average two normalized support forms at a boundary point. A critical midpoint in the average form's supporting face attains level one for both original forms. Uniqueness at critical midpoints makes the two forms equal. Together with support existence and positive normalization, this proves a unique geometric supporting line at every boundary point, without a C1 parametrization assumption.
proved_components.Continuous critical midpoint dynamics: Restrict the compact critical-hexagon parameter family to positive orientation. Shared first midpoints have the same six midpoint coordinates. The first-midpoint projection is a compact quotient map, so the next-midpoint map is continuous on the actual critical midpoint locus. Rotating the labels proves that its second successor is next(p)-p, its third is -p, and its sixth is p. Thus successor is a homeomorphism, all six midpoint coordinates vary continuously, and det(p,next(p))=sqrt(3)/2. No full-boundary coverage or cyclic monotonicity is assumed.
proved_components.Continuous global supporting normal and: Pairs of critical hexagon parameters and positive first-side contacts form a compact set projecting onto the entire minimizer boundary. proved_components.Quantitative support stability and point: Polarizing the exact side-variation quadratic term gives a positive multiple of the squared normal evaluations bounded by the support deficit at the old midpoint.
